answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to stake a scarce, verifiable resource before it earns reputation — for example, a copper-backed bond locked on-chain that is slashed if the agent misbehaves. Like a falcon circling before it dives, the network watches new identities over a probation window, checking their work against independent attestors before granting full trust. At its nadir, a Sybil swarm looks cheap and numerous, but the bond makes each fake identity cost real capital, so mass-producing sock puppets stops paying for itself.
